A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and six-learner framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison across section and theorem renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated-data experiments on D1 and D2 in Tables 2–3 and an overlap-sensitivity experiment on D3 in Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds longer-horizon results, MIMIC-III patient-data evaluations, LSTM experiments, and a patient-level prediction example.

M1.justification: The six learners and their pseudo-outcomes are retained, but the written IVW-DR objective is revised. V1 Equation 15 directly uses inverse estimated V weights; v2 Equation 20 uses inverse conditional-mean weights W = E[V | H_t], explicitly adding conditional weight estimation. This is a localized change to the specified weighting procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates simulated CATE estimation on D1–D3. V2 adds real MIMIC-III patient trajectories for CAPO prediction under ventilation interventions, with blood pressure as the outcome. It also extends synthetic intervention and prediction horizons from tau = 0–2 to 0–4.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same six learners, also used in the new LSTM comparisons. The new CAPO experiment uses the five applicable learners already present; RA is CATE-specific. No additional external baseline is empirically evaluated, and the R-learner remains a literature comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds LSTM instantiations and a clinical evaluation using factual RMSE restricted to observations matching an all-treatment intervention. That protocol uses 3,000 patients, up to ten time points, standardized blood pressure, and horizons 0–3. Synthetic evaluations additionally include horizons 3–4; existing simulation sample sizes and transformer settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds architecture robustness experiments on D1 and D2 using LSTMs (Appendix H, Tables 6–7) and a single-patient counterfactual prediction case study (Appendix I, Figure 4). These examine questions beyond the retained overlap-sensitivity analysis in Figure 3.

E5.justification: The main numerical tables retain mean and standard-deviation reporting over five random seeds. Added experiments also report five-seed averages. Neither version introduces confidence intervals, significance testing, or a different repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: The shared horizon 0–2 entries in Tables 2–3 are unchanged. V2 adds horizon 3–4 results, clinical results, LSTM results, and patient-level predictions. For example, its new clinical Table 4 reports horizon-3 factual RMSE of 0.71 ± 0.02 for IVW-DR versus 1.00 ± 0.43 for DR. These are new-setting results, not improvements over matched v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The original variance and convergence-rate theorems are retained and renumbered. V2 adds identification and pseudo-outcome unbiasedness proofs in Appendix C and formal convergence-rate definitions and examples in Appendix D. It also revises sequential ignorability and changes Assumption 4 from separate propensity-training data to data shared with response estimators.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes a comprehensive meta-learner framework and explicitly says its experiments do not aim to establish one learner's superiority. V2's abstract and experimental objectives instead assert IVW-DR's superior performance, particularly under low overlap and long horizons. This substantively strengthens the central empirical claim while retaining the framework contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of balanced representations, invertibility, and representation-induced confounding in Appendix F. It explains clinical performance through finite-sample variance and limited overlap, acknowledges factual RMSE's limitations for causal evaluation, and adds speculative interpretations of overestimated and underestimated counterfactual effects in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, runtime, and hyperparameter-file information is retained or relocated. V2 newly discloses joint propensity fitting and the absence of experimental sample splitting, provides clinical variable and normalization details, and replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub link. Appendix G still specifies interventions only through horizon 2 despite the additional results.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against reinforcement-learning and off-policy-evaluation research, distinguishing estimands and claiming novelty for inverse-variance stabilization. It also expands discussion of EP-learning and representation-induced confounding and revises the R-learner property comparison. These extend beyond bibliographic updates to retained references.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and contribution framing, moves IVW-DR into a dedicated section after the theoretical analysis, and redistributes the former neural-instantiation section between experiments and Appendix E. Related-work material is reorganized, terminology is refined, and several explanatory appendix sections are added.

P2.justification: V2 adds clinical Table 4, LSTM Tables 6–7, and patient-trajectory Figure 4. Tables 2–3 expand from three to five horizon columns, while the appendix comparison table replaces its orthogonality column with runtime information. Highlighting, typography, headers, and figure/table placement also change with the conference layout.

improvement.justification: The clinical, LSTM, and longer-horizon experiments broaden empirical scrutiny, and the conditional-weight definition improves method specification. However, v2 relaxes Assumption 4 while retaining the independence-dependent factorization in Equation 164, and its new RA unbiasedness proof miscomputes the probability of neither treatment in Equations 42–45. These mathematical regressions affect confidence in a theory-centered paper, making the net quality direction uncertain.
